dedupe_keys.name: nist wildland urban interface fire data collection on structure and parcel vulnerabilities witch creek tanglewood waldo canyon camp fire

description: This NIST programme studies how wildland-urban interface fires ignite buildings and spread through communities, combining post-fire field data collection with laboratory and field experiments to support codes, standards and mitigation. Its case studies cover four major fires: Witch Creek-Guejito (San Diego County, California, 2007), the Tanglewood Complex (Amarillo, Texas, 2011), Waldo Canyon (Colorado Springs, 2012) and the Camp Fire (Butte County, California, 2018). They reconstruct fire behaviour from fuel, weather and terrain, the roles of heat, embers and direct flame contact, the effect of defensive actions, and structure and parcel vulnerabilities. Experiments burn combustible fences, woodpiles and other parcel fuels to quantify their fire and ember exposure and test mitigation. Reported results include the NIST WUI Hazard Mitigation Methodology, life safety guidance for fires that leave no time to evacuate, and the Camp Fire analysis of spot fires, fire spread pathways, burnovers and temporary refuge areas. Coverage: four US fires between 2007 and 2018, plus laboratory work. Access: the project page links to per-fire and per-topic pages and NIST reports. Licence: public information from NIST; free. Caveats: the page summarises the programme; building-level data sit in separate reports, and future deployments are planned. Simulation uses are structure ignition and parcel fuel rules for wildfire spread and exposure models and for mitigation planning. Related records: the NIST Fire Calorimetry Database, the California wildfire building damage and Chapter 7A records; the services piece holds the Camp Fire evacuation case study.
